The D-293 sentence gets none of that. There is no path, no digest, no heading line, no commit, and no verbatim quotation block for it anywhere in v9. The asymmetry is visible inside /basedOn itself: v9 newly adds basedOn.recording 'D-105' and basedOn.commit '36949e33e3f72f51c654805b903a487b30fd6660' to pin the provenance of the PREDECESSOR's recording - both of which I verified (COORD line 4122 '## D-105 - Record signed-index-trust-contract.v8 as DR-112's accepted design-contract candidate', and git shows 36949e3 'D-105: record signed-index-trust-contract.v8 as DR-112 candidate'). Consequence: a later reader cannot tell from the artifact which COORD state Decision 6 was read from, cannot detect if D-293 is later superseded, and cannot reproduce the verbatim claim without going outside the artifact. That is precisely the failure mode the carryDiscipline and locationDiscipline fields exist to prevent.

whyItIsAProblem: Two things are gone: the word 'Closed' before 'roster', and the closure sentence 'Every path neither the roster nor succession metadata names is unchanged from v7.'

That sentence is what turns a list into a claim. Without it the artifact states which paths it changed but never states that it changed no others, so the roster is unfalsifiable from the artifact's own text.

This lineage's standing reviewer instruction depends on the closure. reviewGuidance carries 'Attack any silent v1-to-v2 path outside honestyRepairsFromV1 / basedOn.method' (index 13) and the same attack again at 24, 31, 38, 44, 52 and 57 for each later step. That attack only bites if basedOn.method declares the roster closed.

The claim happens to be true - I verified it - but a successor that relies on the reviewer to establish its own honesty guarantee has moved the burden the wrong way, and the next successor inherits the weaker form.
shouldFix.howIChecked: I flattened both artifacts to leaf paths and compared. 20 leaves differ; every one is covered by one of the 12 roster tokens; nothing is removed; the sole top-level addition is honestyRepairsFromV8, which the roster names. I separately confirmed /machine, /fixtureClasses, /trustPolicyShape, /recoveryAuthorityShape, /recoveryCeremony, /auditAndWaiver, /airGapPayload, /roles, /monotonicStore, /identityDependencies, /reviewGuidance, /recordedInputs, /reMeasurementAtV4, /trustTextCarriedVerbatim, /offlineTextCarriedVerbatim are identical to v8, and that /offlineRunningPolicy is identical apart from the one rostered cell. shouldFix.title: The residual is described as a question of 'wording', but 'preview' is a product-stage scope term everywhere else in this artifact. Under the artifact's own vocabulary v9 leaves the refusal's scope less determined than v8 did, and that weakening is not recorded.
whyItIsAProblem: Everywhere else in v9, 'preview' names the preview product stage, not a form of words. roles[0..2].preview = 'in G08 install scope'; roles[3].preview = 'named; not a required preview shipping surface'; roles[4].preview = 'DEFERRED with DR-110. Named so the role is not silent.'; airGapPayload.repairMaterialStanding = 'A preview payload may omit repair material only as a typed absence, never as a silent hole that triggers download.'; reviewGuidance[6] = 'Attack designing replay or repair-media as if in preview.' In that vocabulary 'preview' answers WHERE a rule applies.

Read in that vocabulary, v8's cell 'refuse unless OD-112-3 is later numbered; preview refuse' and v8's standing 'RESERVED. Preview refuse. Not minted.' are scope statements: in preview, refuse; the general number is reserved. That reading is coherent and it is the only one consistent with the rest of the document.

v9 recasts the same token as a wording variant: totalDecision[4].alreadyRunning says 'Residual wording of the refusal (plain refuse versus preview refuse) is named, not chosen', and namedOpenDecisions[2].standing says 'Residual wording of whether the word preview remains'. Under the artifact's established use, 'plain refuse' versus 'preview refuse' is not two ways of saying one thing - it is refuse-everywhere versus refuse-in-preview.

The consequence runs against the sentence v9 exists to carry. D-293 says OD-112-3 is the FINAL fail-closed policy. If the open token is scope, then leaving 'plain refuse versus preview refuse' unchosen leaves open whether the fail-closed policy reaches beyond preview - which is in tension with 'final'. v8 at least stated 'Preview refuse' flatly; on the scope axis the successor is less determined than the predecessor it succeeds, and honestyRepairsFromV8 records the supersession of the 'unless OD-112-3 is later numbered' clause but records no such weakening.

The remaining cells make the contrast plain. Every other alreadyRunning cell carries an operative token - 'refuse', 'refuse (do not treat survival as trust)', 'continue', 'continue already-installed verified component processes'. Row 4 is now the only cell in a table named totalDecision that carries commentary in place of a decision token. The refusal itself is still recoverable - the row keeps refusalReason 'CONTINUE-COMPONENT-NOT-TRUSTED', and auditAndWaiver.audit makes refusalReason 'REQUIRED exactly when outcome=refused' - so the table is still total. It is the scope of that refusal that the new text leaves in the air.
shouldFix.howIChecked: I enumerated every occurrence of 'preview' in v9 (10 occurrences across 8 paths) and classified each. Every occurrence outside the two rostered cells and the two authorityClaim/purpose restatements uses it as a product-stage term. I also confirmed neither v8 reviewer's frozen verdict discusses the token, so this reading has not previously been settled on the record.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: State, in the artifact's own vocabulary, which axis is residual - the wording of the refusal message, or the stage scope of the refusal - and if it is the scope axis, record in honestyRepairsFromV8 that v8's flat 'Preview refuse' scope statement is being reopened, so the successor is not silently less determined than its predecessor. Alternatively use a token that is not already load-bearing as a stage name.
shouldFix.notWhatIAmAsking: I am NOT choosing the residual and this finding does not require it to be chosen. Naming which axis is open is a naming act; picking plain refuse or preview refuse is the choice I am forbidden to make and am not making.
